clue.text: On the face of it, it is the quickest way to fall in love

definitions.meaning: judging by appearances, on first impression

definitions.text: the quickest way to fall in love
definitions.meaning: love conceived the very moment two people first set eyes on each other

explanation.surface: A remark that, apparently, instant attraction is the fastest route to romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idiom: apparently, on first viewing; and the phrase used of love that strikes on a single glance.

clue.text: Solvent public school investing in service which cannot be returned

indicators.note: investing in is read as going inside, so the school sits within the tennis serve

parts.note: an ace in tennis is a serve the opponent cannot touch
Eton is the famous English public (fee-paying) school

explanation.surface: A school putting money into a service that offers no comeback, as if it were solvent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solvent' looks like 'financially sound' beside 'investing', but it is the chemical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Nail-polish remover is a familiar chemical solvent of this kind.

clue.text: A priest, physically nimble, but likely to crack

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
agile means quick and nimble in movement

explanation.surface: A spry clergyman who nevertheless seems close to breaking down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brittle or delicate is easily broken or cracked.

clue.text: Barker from Ireland describes the sinking sun

definitions.meaning: a dog breed from Ireland with a chestnut coat
read literally, a crimson sun going down below the horizon

explanation.surface: An Irish dog seems to be painting a sunset scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish breed of gundog is named for its colour; a red sun dropping at dusk is literally that colour going down.

clue.text: Not 100 mph

parts.note: the clue word written upward, as a down entry is, gives the letters of a hundred followed by up

explanation.surface: A denial that something was going at a hundred miles an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer is an instruction, 'TON up', that turns TON upwards into the clue word 'Not'. TON UP is British slang for doing 100 mph, especially on a motorbike.
explanation.definitionFit: A ton is slang for a hundred, so the phrase means reaching a speed of one hundred.

clue.text: Real understanding is not far off

definitions.meaning: deep perception into the nature of something
close enough to be seen, read as two words

explanation.surface: Genuine comprehension is close at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Perception into the truth of something is one sense; as two words, visible and so near, is the other.

clue.text: Homer on dispensing a drug banned by Olympic rulers

definitions.text: a drug banned by Olympic rulers

indicators.note: a pharmacist dispensing a drug gives the letters out and makes them up anew

explanation.surface: The poet Homer handing out a substance outlawed by the Olympic authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homer' suggests the Greek poet and so Olympus, but it is simply fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Growth hormone and similar substances are prohibited performance enhancers in sport.

clue.text: Makea stab in the dark-with a cannabis filled hypodermic

definitions.meaning: make a wild guess or random attempt

explanation.surface: Guessing blindly, aided by a syringe loaded with dope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makea' is the printed 'Make a'. POT is slang for cannabis and a SHOT is an injection, so a pot shot is literally a cannabis-filled hypodermic.
explanation.definitionFit: A random shot fired without aim is a hit-or-miss attempt; read literally the phrase is an injection of marijuana.

clue.text: The tragic lover who grew a beard about 50

indicators.note: about places the beard words around the number, holding it inside

parts.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A doomed romantic hero who grew facial hair around the age of fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Abelard was the medieval scholar whose love affair with Heloise ended in his castration.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval philosopher is famed for his ill-fated romance with his pupil Heloise.

clue.text: Literary celebrity took a turn around the street for a breather

indicators.note: around puts the turned word on both sides of the street's letters
turning round means the celebrity's word is read backwards

parts.note: a literary lion is a celebrated author
Str is an abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A famous writer strolled around the block to get some fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took a turn' turns the celebrity backwards to NOIL. A literary lion is a much-feted writer; 'a breather' is a playful way of naming an air passage.
explanation.definitionFit: Each opening of the nose is a passage through which one inhales.

clue.text: From day to day, to the of recorded time' (Macbeth)

definitions.text: From day to day, to the of recorded time' (Macbeth)

parts.words: From day to day, to the of recorded time' (Macbeth)
parts.note: a quotation with a gap: the missing words complete Macbeth's 'Tomorrow, and tomorrow' speech

explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth's speech runs 'Creeps in this petty pace from day to day, / To the ___ of recorded time': the answer fills the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: The final unit of sound in the speech is where recorded time ends, in Shakespeare's image.

clue.text: Piccadilly figure I have found to be somewhat caustic

parts.note: the statue in London's Piccadilly Circus is popularly called Eros
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone reports finding a statue in central London rather biting.
explanation.walkthrough: Piccadilly Circus is a famous road junction in central London, topped by a winged statue known as Eros.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that wears away by degrees is mildly corrosive.

clue.text: Age about which pigs might fly

definitions.note: a description of birds rather than a noun: they are creatures that may take wing

indicators.note: about makes the animals' word go around the period of time

parts.note: an eon is an age, a very long period

explanation.surface: A playful nod to the saying that pigs might fly, as if the time had come.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on 'pigs might fly' (said of something impossible), but the flyers are birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Doves and their relatives are birds that take wing, unlike swine.

clue.text: Only part of the performer's programme

definitions.meaning: a portion or fragment of a whole
an item a musician or actor presents in a recital

explanation.surface: A musician plays just a section of the planned repertoire.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment or bit is one sense; a musical or dramatic work in a recital is the other.

clue.text: Part time office girl has hair style to make one look seductive

definitions.note: an adjective for a noun: the answer is a seductive woman, and 'to make one look' leads into it

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
a tress is a lock or plait of hair

explanation.surface: A temporary secretary does her hair to look alluring.
explanation.definitionFit: An enticing woman who sets out to allure is a siren or vamp.

clue.text: Car demo to be organised apparently

definitions.text: Car demo to be organised apparently

indicators.note: to be organised means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A protest drive that has supposedly been arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: A car demonstration that has been organised looks like a procession of cars; 'apparently' admits the whole clue is a picture of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal procession of cars, often escorting a dignitary, is a planned parade of vehicles.

clue.text: Is it so confidential that it must be kept only in one's head?

definitions.text: Is it so confidential that it must be kept only in one's head?

parts.words: Is it so confidential that it must be kept only in one's head?
parts.note: something classified at the highest level, and the head is the top of the body, so a secret kept up there

explanation.surface: Wondering whether information is so sensitive it can never be written down.
explanation.definitionFit: Information of the highest classification is secret at the very top level.

clue.text: Would an airman consider it to be a flop on Shrove Tuesday?

definitions.text: Would an airman consider it to be a flop on Shrove Tuesday?

parts.words: Would an airman consider it to be a flop on Shrove Tuesday?
parts.note: a pilot's term for a flat belly landing, and the flat batter dish tossed on Shrove Tuesday

explanation.surface: A pilot wondering whether a dish on Shrove Tuesday is a failure.
explanation.walkthrough: Shrove Tuesday, before Lent, is called Pancake Day in Britain. A pilot's crash-landing on the aircraft's belly is called by the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat landing where the aircraft drops flat is named after the flat batter dish of Shrove Tuesday.

clue.text: Eastern reason for action is charged with sentiment

parts.note: a motive is what drives someone to act

explanation.surface: An Oriental explanation for behaviour is full of feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Language arousing strong feeling is emotionally loaded.

clue.text: Lens' point of interest

parts.note: the spot where a lens brings light rays together, and the phrase for a centre of attention

explanation.definitionFit: The point at which a lens converges light is its focus, and a centre of attention is a point of the same name.

clue.text: Feverish anger is apparent after a month

indicators.note: after puts the anger word behind the month's letters

parts.note: Feb is the abbreviation for February
to rile is to anger

explanation.surface: Fevered irritation shows up once a few weeks have passed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word derives from the Latin for fever and also means nervously excited.

clue.text: Seizes criminals by their necks?

parts.note: police slang for arresting someone, and literally grabbing them by the neckband of a shirt

explanation.definitionFit: To arrest a suspect is slang for grabbing them by the neckband of a shirt.

clue.text: Dry laundry for a somewhat down-market place of residence

definitions.meaning: peg washing on a line to air

definitions.text: a somewhat down-market place of residence
definitions.meaning: an informal word for a haunt or seedy dwelling

explanation.surface: Drying the washing to escape a rather shabby home.
explanation.definitionFit: Pegging washing on a line is one sense; a favourite haunt or dive is the other.

clue.text: Buy someone a meal to alleviate his complaint

definitions.meaning: pay for another's dinner as a gift
give medical care for an illness

explanation.surface: Taking a sick friend out to dinner to cheer them up.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying for someone else's food is one sense; giving medical care for an ailment is the other.

clue.text: Give Eleanor massage treatment for a fever rash

parts.note: a rub is a massage
Ella is a short form of Eleanor

explanation.surface: Advice to massage a woman to ease her feverish spots.
explanation.definitionFit: German measles is a mild viral illness marked by fever and a red rash.

clue.text: When one may take food within the hour

definitions.text: When one may take food within the hour

indicators.note: within places the eating word inside the word for the hour

parts.note: the hour is the time, as in 'what's the hour?'
to eat is to take food

explanation.surface: Explaining when food can be had within the next sixty minutes.
explanation.definitionFit: The late-afternoon meal hour is the period set aside for a light meal.

clue.text: The servant girl makes a great complaint

parts.note: big means great in size
an ail is an ailment or complaint

explanation.surface: The maid is making a huge fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: An abigail is an old word for a lady's maid, from a character in Beaumont and Fletcher's The Scornful Lady.
explanation.definitionFit: The name became a dated generic word for a lady's maid.

clue.text: Always more, whatever else may be said

definitions.meaning: read as three words, at no time a smaller amount
all the same, in spite of that

explanation.surface: Insisting on ever-greater amounts regardless of objections.
explanation.definitionFit: Split into three words it means at no point smaller, hence always more; whole, it means however or all the same.
